highlights.description: Default-deny dependency policy engine: an authored policy.json declares which components may directly depend on which others, a scanner produces a graph.json of what actually exists, and a pure evaluator reports where reality diverges from intent — with a ratchet mode so enforcement starts before historical coupling is fully classified

Ecosystem-neutral component model: Go modules, directories within them (proto-modules), npm packages, crates, container images, and services are all locatable components; Go ships as the first and reference scanner

Tier system with explicit, non-transitive allow-lists plus deny patterns that can reach third-party targets (e.g. "an abstraction core must not import provider SDKs"), layered over per-component foundation status
Full enforcement surface: eleven CLI commands, a go/analysis analyzer reporting violations at the offending import line, a composite GitHub Action, and a self-contained multi-page HTML report

added.description: Component model with longest-prefix locator resolution and status semantics (governed, foundation, deprecated, ungoverned)
Dependency graph document types with evidence provenance (source-import, manifest), scan-level metadata, edge merging, and graph-to-graph diffing
Policy document types and pure evaluator: scope patterns, reason-required relationships, expirable exceptions, tier rules with mayDependOn/mayNotDependOn, four-state findings
JSON Schemas generated from the policy and graph Go types, embedded for non-Go consumers
Go scanners: go.mod manifests, ImportsOnly source imports, bounded-concurrency multi-root scanning with a shared component registry, and GitHub-API fleet scanning with no cloning
Analytics tables (Policy/Actual/Difference as flat JSON/CSV) and a self-contained multi-page HTML report with an interactive org-grouped dependency graph
deppolicy CLI: scan, scan-github, check, diff (ratchet), policy-diff, validate, promote, report, export (Mermaid/DOT), tables, and ui
go/analysis analyzer and deppolicy-vet binary for standalone and go vet -vettool use

documentation.description: README, normative SPEC.md, repo CLAUDE.md, and MIT license
README repositioned as ecosystem-neutral with Go as the reference scanner, plus an Extending Beyond Go section
MkDocs documentation site: concepts, guides, and reference across twelve pages
